cheng: Ran a stressshot across an H100/L40S mixed cluster this morning. Weird kernel-selector oscillation around seq=1024, bs=8 — end-to-end latency spikes ~2–3x. posting raw run and logs :eyes:

olivia: ugh, can you paste the exact command / run-id so we can reproduce?

cheng: run-id=2026-03-stressshot-42
command: ./bench_attn --gpus h100,l40s --kernels fused,paged,flashv2 --seq 64,256,512,1024,2048 --bs 1,4,8,16 --kv-cache=on --runs=5 --seed=42

sample stdout (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-18 07:14:02] seq=1024 bs=8 kernel=fused throughput=118 tok/s p50=46.2ms p95=212.4ms p99=571.9ms
[2026-03-18 07:14:05] seq=1024 bs=8 kernel=paged  throughput=302 tok/s p50=17.9ms p95=88.5ms  p99=122.1ms
[2026-03-18 07:14:09] seq=1024 bs=8 kernel=fused  throughput=126 tok/s p50=43.1ms p95=198.0ms p99=540.3ms
[2026-03-18 07:14:12] seq=1024 bs=8 kernel=paged  throughput=311 tok/s p50=16.5ms p95=85.2ms  p99=118.7ms
```

cheng: selector logs show it flipping every 2–3 iterations: `kernel_selector: pick=fused reason=mem_est_overflow` then `pick=paged reason=latency_target`. Means estimation boundary is jittery and we're paying warmup / memcpy costs when swapping kernels.

kai: do you have profiler flame or nvprof counters? sounds like eviction/prefetch pattern.

cheng: attached short flame sampling from nvtx and lightweight perf: (pasted inline)
```
Top hotspots (sample %)
attn_fused_forward        42%  
page_eviction_worker     18%  
kv_cache_prefetch        12%  
cudaMemcpyAsync           9%  
softmax_kernel            7%  
other kernels             12%
```
Observations: eviction shows up only in fused runs; paged runs push eviction into background and keep forward kernel leaner.

mike: hypothesis: a prefetch/paged threshold change in the selector made mem_est conservative. The oscillation boundary at seq=1024/bs=8 may be where mem_est crosses the fused->paged heuristic. Can we repro with forced kernels?

cheng: yes. ran quick A/B: `--kernel-force=paged` vs `--kernel-force=fused` on same hardware:
```
seq=1024 bs=8 paged  throughput=305 tok/s p95=90ms p99=125ms
seq=1024 bs=8 fused  throughput=120 tok/s p95=205ms p99=530ms
```
So forcing paged avoids the spike. Also observed increased host<->device memcpy in fused case.

olivia: great repro. can you attach a perf trace + kernel logs to the bug? assign to eng-runtime for bisect.

perf-bot: Automated summary created: https://perf.redwood.local/d/abc123/attn-stressshot-2026-03-42  (dash snapshot, seq sweep, bs sweep, selector toggles). CI test matrix hit: h100-l40s mixed region. Related commits to check: abc123..def456 (kernel selector heuristics), maybe also gh-ml/quant-prefetch commit.

kai: next steps I suggest:
- bisect selector heuristic using the smaller commit window (abc123..def456)
- run forced-kernel A/B across full seq sweep (64..2048) to validate boundary
- add a short cool-down to selector (sticky picks) to avoid flip-flop while we tune mem_est

mike: I can run the bisect tonight on the H100 pool. cheng, can you upload the full nvtx trace and the gdb backtrace for the eviction worker?

cheng: will upload trace.tar.gz to the incident bucket and kick off the bisect. link: s3://redwood-perf/2026/03/stressshot-42/trace.tar.gz  (contains nvprof, nvtx, stdout logs).

olivia: thanks — please @kai @mike when uploads complete. once we have the bisect result we'll decide whether to change mem_est or add sticky selection. :thumbsup:

cheng: upload done, kicked bisect job (job-id=bisect-7744). i'll post results here when ready. :rocket:
